text:
nora: Hey team  throwing this out there early: we're pursuing an international adoption and I expect to be out ~10 weeks starting Mar 15. Two parts: 6 weeks in-country for placement (country TBD) then 4 weeks back home. Main concerns: 1) any tax credits or adoption expense reimbursement process through benefits? 2) payroll implications if I'm technically outside the US for more than 30 days; do I need a payroll transfer? 3) what paperwork does People Ops need to approve the placement leave? 4) can I keep my laptop and hotspot while abroad?

michelle (People Ops): Huge congrats Nora! Short answers: 1) Adoption expense reimbursement is part of the benefits plan but has a claims process and caps; Emma from Benefits will share the claim form and eligible expense list. 2) Payroll: if you remain on US payroll for <90 days we often keep US withholding; beyond that Payroll may need to register or arrange a contractor payment. We'll route to Jules for a nexus check. 3) People Ops needs the Parental/Adoption Leave Request form with placement letter and court docs; mark date segments and country. 4) IT allows devices abroad with an Equipment Travel ticket; check export rules with IT.

jules (Payroll): Hi Nora  quick detail: please upload the adoption placement letter, proposed travel dates, and passport copy. We'll run a payroll-country-nexus check. If the country requires local payroll for >30 days of presence or any work is performed, we may need to set up local payroll or do a contractor payment, which affects taxes and benefits. I'll DM a short intake form.

emma (Benefits): From Benefits side: adoption reimbursement covers eligible adoption fees up to the cap (see plan SPD). You must submit receipts and a placement confirmation. If you are on leave and remain an active employee, health coverage continues; if payroll moves to a local country we need to confirm benefit eligibility and premium collection. I'll share the adoption claim PDF and timeline.

visa-team: Note for international placements: some countries require a local guardian or sponsor during placement; confirm with the adoption agency. Also check travel visa timing as some consulates require a consular approval before leaving. This can affect your leave dates.

michelle (People Ops): Practical checklist for Nora:
- Submit Parental/Adoption Leave Request by Feb 20
- Upload placement letter + court docs + passport copy
- Notify manager to approve coverage/backfill
- Open Equipment Travel ticket with IT if taking devices
- Run nexus check with Payroll once docs uploaded

nora: Thanks! Manager will coordinate backfill. One nuance: I may do a day or two of occasional email triage from placement location  not full work. Does that change payroll?

jules (Payroll): Occasional email/phone checks are typically okay and don't create local employment presence, but anything compensated or scheduled work (oncall, sprints, meetings billed as work time) can. Please capture expected activities on the intake form so we model risk.

emma (Benefits): Also note: adoption tax credits are on your personal tax return (Form 8839 historically), not the company's benefits claims. We can provide documentation but you should consult a tax advisor on timing. Benefits reimbursement is separate and requires receipts and a placement confirmation.

it-bot: Reminder: Equipment Travel requests must be submitted at least 10 business days prior to international shipping. Link: https://redwood.internal/it/equipment-travel.

michelle (People Ops): Action items: Nora  submit leave request + docs by Feb 20; Jules  payroll to run nexus check after docs; Emma  send adoption reimbursement claim form; Manager  post backfill plan. We'll reconvene if the country is named so we can map specifics.

nora: Form submitted and placement letter uploaded (placeholder country: pending). Opened IT ticket IT-8123 for device travel. Thanks all  will update when agency confirms country.

jules (Payroll): Received docs. We'll run the initial risk check and post back by Feb 28. If country ends up requiring local payroll, we'll outline options (local payroll vs contractor payment vs short-term secondment).

michelle (People Ops): Awesome. Congrats again Nora  we'll support the logistics. If country is in EU/UK/APAC that usually has established flows; less common jurisdictions take extra time. Keep us posted.
